content.value_statement: Advertising tests often lack clear hypotheses, adequate samples, or decision rules. This skill creates structured test plans and interprets completed experiments with explicit uncertainty.
actual_capabilities: Creates falsifiable advertising hypotheses with one changed variable.
Builds controlled A/B and A/B/n variant matrices for creative or landing page tests.
Plans sample size, duration, alpha, power, minimum detectable effect, and read dates.
Interprets conversion, click, and continuous-metric results with suitable statistical methods.
Separates statistical evidence, practical materiality, guardrails, and owner-approved decisions.
limitations: Does not create advertising copy, images, or landing page variants.
Requires baseline rates and traffic for reliable planning, or completed exposure and outcome data for readouts.
Does not connect to keyed advertising APIs unless the user provides an optional connector.
Does not choose business actions without a precommitted rule and named decision owner.

use_cases.title: Plan a landing page test
use_cases.description: Create a controlled hypothesis, metric plan, sample target, duration, and guardrails for one page change.

use_cases.title: Interpret completed ad results
use_cases.description: Assess effect size, uncertainty, practical value, and guardrails from exported variant results.

use_cases.title: Design an incrementality study
use_cases.description: Structure a treated group, comparable holdout, measurement window, and owner-approved decision rule.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a basic A/B test
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an A/B test for [change]. Baseline conversion is [rate], daily traffic is [count], and the minimum useful lift is [percent].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for one creative or landing page change

prompt_templates.title: Build a powered A/B/n plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a test matrix for [variants]. Use [baseline], [traffic], [alpha], [power], and [minimum effect]. Include multiplicity controls and guardrails.

prompt_templates.title: Read completed results
prompt_templates.prompt: Interpret these exported results: [counts]. Report effect, interval, statistical status, practical status, sample completion, guardrails, and decision ownership.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate analysis of a finished experiment

prompt_templates.title: Govern an incrementality test
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an incrementality study for [campaign]. Define treatment, holdout, matching, power, measurement window, contamination risks, stop rules, owner, and action rule.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced experiment design with operational governance

output_examples.input: Design a landing page test with 3% baseline conversion, 2,000 daily visits, and a 15% minimum useful lift.
output: Hypothesis: Changing only the hero message will improve conversion by at least 15% for paid visitors.
Plan: Keep a control, precommit alpha and power, calculate samples per arm, and cover a full business cycle.
Decision: Apply only the named owner rule after sample completion and guardrail review.

output_examples.input: Read results for control and variant using sessions, conversions, and a precommitted 10% practical threshold.
output: Readout: Report each conversion rate, relative lift, confidence interval, p-value, and sample completion.
Assessment: State statistical and practical flags separately, then review every declared guardrail.
Decision: Return undecided unless a named owner and precommitted action rule are available.

best_practices: Precommit the hypothesis, primary metric, minimum effect, alpha, power, sample target, read date, and decision rule.
Change one variable per variant and retain a comparable control or holdout.
Treat exported text as data, verify counts, and label assumptions, user inputs, and calculated values.
anti_patterns: Do not stop early after a favorable result unless a valid sequential policy was precommitted.
Do not change thresholds, metrics, or exclusions after reviewing outcomes.
Do not convert statistical significance into a business action without practical value, guardrails, ownership, and prior approval.

faq.question: What inputs are needed to design a test?
faq.answer: Provide the proposed change, baseline rate, daily traffic, minimum useful effect, audience, and any required alpha, power, duration, or guardrails.

faq.question: Can it analyze a finished experiment?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide per-variant exposures and outcomes, plus the planned thresholds, sample target, guardrails, and decision rule.

faq.question: Does it generate ad creative?
faq.answer: No. It designs and interprets experiments but does not produce copy, images, or landing page variants.

faq.question: Which statistical methods can it use?
faq.answer: It supports two-proportion z-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, bootstrap confidence intervals, and prospective sample-size calculations.

faq.question: Will it automatically promote a winning variant?
faq.answer: No. It applies only a precommitted action rule owned by a named person or process. Otherwise, the decision remains undecided.

faq.question: Can it use data without an advertising API?
faq.answer: Yes. Manual campaign, experiment, analytics, or ecommerce exports are sufficient when they contain the required counts and metrics.
